364	//

366	// forks or clones the project inherits it. Honoring it blindly would push a
367	// contributor's session data into the upstream project's checkpoint repo — which
368	// they typically cannot write to and should not be writing to. This is the check

372	//
373	//  1. A checkpoint_remote in .entire/settings.local.json is gitignored and
374	//     per-clone, so it cannot have been inherited — it is always ours.
375	//  2. Otherwise, compare the CHECKPOINT repo's owner against ORIGIN's owner:

392	// those repos. settings.local.json is the escape hatch when the checkpoint repo
393	// is genuinely ours but owned by a different account or org than origin.

398			// which skipped the check rather than blocking on it.
399			return false, ""
400		}
401		if settings.CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly(ctx) {

405		// Origin identifies the repo we are working in. Without one, the push remote
406		// is the only identity available, and using it is what the predecessor
407		// effectively did — a repo whose only remote is e.g. "upstream" must not lose
408		// its configured checkpoint remote just because nothing is named "origin".
409		// There is no origin-vs-push-remote divergence to worry about in that case:
410		// the repo has exactly one identity.
411		identityURL, identitySource := originURL, "origin"
412		if identityURL == "" {
413			identityURL, identitySource = pushRemoteURL, "push remote"
414		}
415		if identityURL == "" {
416			return true, "no remote to establish ownership"
417		}

419		info, err := ParseURL(identityURL)
420		if err != nil || info.Owner == "" {
421			return true, identitySource + " URL owner could not be determined"
422		}
423		if strings.EqualFold(info.Owner, checkpointOwner) {
424			return false, ""
425		}

455	func deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info *Info, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) (string, error) {
456		switch info.Protocol {
457		case ProtocolSSH:

459			// port is set (e.g., from ssh://git@host:2222/...), use the ssh:// URL form.

462			}

464		case ProtocolHTTPS:
465			return fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/%s.git", info.HostPort(), config.Repo), nil
466		case ProtocolEntire:
467			// entire:// push-through mirrors are cluster-scoped: keep the cluster
468			// host and forge segment, swap in the checkpoint repo. Only derivable
469			// when the forge maps back to the configured provider's host, so a
470			// github checkpoint_remote never routes through another forge's mirror.
471			host, ok := providerHost(config.Provider)

473				return "", fmt.Errorf("entire:// remote forge %q does not match checkpoint provider %q", info.Forge, config.Provider)

492	//     so checkpoints use the same auth the user already has for that endpoint.
493	//  3. Otherwise SSH on the provider host.

496	// usable signal), in which case the caller falls back to the origin remote.

498		repo, err := openRepoAt(ctx, dir)

528				return &Info{Protocol: info.Protocol, Host: info.Host, Port: info.Port}, true
529			}

532		// 3. Default to SSH on the provider host.

543	// go-git's extension check. gitrepo.OpenCurrent resolves the worktree root from

545	// open) when no explicit root is given.
546	func openRepoAt(ctx context.Context, dir string) (*git.Repository, error) {

562	// remote (in deterministic name order) whose host matches host and whose
563	// protocol is a usable git transport (ssh/https). entire:// and other
564	// non-transport remotes are ignored.
565	func findRemoteInfoForHost(repo *git.Repository, host string) (*Info, bool) {
566		cfg, err := repo.Config()
567		if err != nil {
568			return nil, false
569		}
570		names := make([]string, 0, len(cfg.Remotes))
571		for name := range cfg.Remotes {
572			names = append(names, name)
573		}
574		sort.Strings(names)
575		for _, name := range names {
576			for _, rawURL := range cfg.Remotes[name].URLs {
577				info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(rawURL)
578				if err != nil {
579					continue
580				}
581				if strings.EqualFold(info.Host, host) && isDirectGitTransport(info.Protocol) {

20	// BACKFILL's absence probe. Write paths run inside git hooks (post-commit,
21	// stop-time finalize) where a dead network must not stall the user's
22	// workflow for the read path's full fetch window; combined with the
23	// per-store failure memo in the git-refs store, a loop over N checkpoints

28	// the historical FetchCheckpointRef behavior).

32	// data is fetched from. It prefers the effective URL resolved by FetchURL,
33	// which is the source of truth for checkpoint fetch location. If URL
34	// resolution fails, it falls back to the origin remote name so callers can
35	// still attempt a fetch.

61	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) from the checkpoint remote into the
62	// local ref of the same name, so the git-refs store can resolve a checkpoint
63	// written on another machine.

65	// Contract — absence is distinguishable from failure:
66	//   - The remote genuinely lacking the ref returns an error wrapping
67	//     plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound (probed via ls-remote before fetching,
68	//     because `git fetch` of a missing refspec fails indistinguishably from a
69	//     transport error). Store probes classify this as "checkpoint not found",
70	//     which write routing may legitimately act on.
71	//   - Any transport-level failure (probe or fetch) is surfaced as a real
72	//     error, never mapped to absence — a false "absent" would misdirect a
73	//     backfill onto another backend instead of retrying.
74	//   - A repository with no git remotes at all and no checkpoint_remote
75	//     configured also returns an error wrapping plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound
76	//     without probing: there is no remote that could host the ref.

88		// remoteless repo is misreported as a transport outage. Absence is only
89		// ever classified on positive evidence; each escape below keeps today's
90		// hard-failure probe:

98		//   - any remote listed, or the listing itself failing: checkpoint refs
